sources.title: Higher curvature counter terms cause the bounce in loop cosmology

evidence.text: Does the loop-cosmology bounce follow uniquely from quantization, or from an ambiguous finite-difference modification of the Hamiltonian? The paper asks whether choices of polymerization function correspond to undetermined higher-curvature terms in a covariant action.

evidence.text: Can quantum-gravity higher-curvature terms relax geodesic focusing and singularity-theorem conditions? The paper distinguishes nonperturbative quadratic gravity from general relativity treated perturbatively as an effective field theory.

sources.title: Higher curvature counter terms cause the bounce in loop cosmology

evidence.text: Construct alternative regulators from linear combinations of finite translation operators, compare their small-β Taylor coefficients, and study zeros of f′ in the resulting classical Hamilton equations. An infinite sine-series example is used to challenge generic singularity resolution.

sources.title: Singularity avoidance in quantum gravity

evidence.text: Analyze the Raychaudhuri discriminant Δ = Rμνkμkν. With twist discarded, positive contributions favor focusing and negative contributions can favor defocusing; the paper studies these contributions rather than constructing complete spacetime solutions.

sources.title: Higher curvature counter terms cause the bounce in loop cosmology

evidence.text: Retain the vanishing Hamiltonian constraint rather than merely the conserved energy of the gauge-fixed Lagrangian. Factor the constraint and compute ratios of Hamiltonian flows to obtain the gauge-invariant evolution dv/dφ.

sources.title: Higher curvature counter terms cause the bounce in loop cosmology

evidence.text: Legendre-transform the modified Hamiltonian explicitly for f=sin. Relate the resulting expansion in powers of ȧ/a to curvature invariants using traces R(n) of Ricci-tensor powers, integration by parts and an appendix induction in conformal time.

sources.title: Singularity avoidance in quantum gravity

evidence.text: For quadratic gravity, transform to explicit massive-field variables, trace-reverse the metric equations and contract with a timelike tangent. Two approximations are used: the isotropic ansatz φμν = φgμν/4, and small massive-field perturbations about an arbitrary spacetime.

sources.title: Singularity avoidance in quantum gravity

evidence.text: For EFT gravity, expand the effective equations and discriminant to leading order in the metric perturbation, retaining local quadratic-curvature terms and nonlocal log(−□/μ²) operators. Timelike and null congruences are considered separately.
